notes: A security fix worth taking. Crisp runs a small local helper so the editor can play your clips; until this build that helper would hand any file in your home folder to anything on your Mac that asked it over the loopback address — including a web page open in your browser. It could not read the contents back, but it could learn which files you have. It now answers only Crisp itself, and only for video and audio files you have actually opened. Nothing about your footage ever left your Mac, before or after. Also: asking to level only part of a clip now says Crisp works on the whole clip instead of quietly levelling all of it, "slow it down to a third" slows to a third rather than a half, and levelled audio no longer pins at full scale.
